result:
New top-level `src/smoother.rs` (exported as `kalman_filters::smoother`, re-exported as `{rts_smooth, Smoothed}`), with 16 tests in `tests/rts_smoother_tests.rs`, one module line in `src/lib.rs`, and only `pub(crate)` on `rel_tol`/`diagonal` in `src/filter.rs`. Top-level rather than under `linear`, because `linear` is an alias of `filter.rs`, so a method there would make the filter depend on the smoother. DESIGN_NOTES.md updated; frozen files untouched.
Approach: the forward pass runs `predict`/`update` on a clone of the filter, storing filtered x/P in flat row-major Vecs; the backward pass overwrites step k in place once smoothed, recomputing each predicted prior with the same in-place calls `predict` uses, and gets the gain as Gᵀ = P_{k+1|k}⁻¹ F P_{k|k} by `Cholesky::solve_mut` (never inverting), reusing update's 100ε relative pivot test; failure returns `SingularMatrix`.
Easy: `model()` plus `Clone` let the forward pass be the filter's own `predict`/`update` on a clone, and the in-place gemm/gemv/quadform calls and Option-wrapped Cholesky idiom carried into the backward step with fixed step-sized buffers.
Hard: the filter never forms an inverse but the RTS gain needs P_{k+1|k}⁻¹: solved through Cholesky and reports SingularMatrix, a policy the spec does not define (a pseudo-inverse could smooth degenerate models such as P0 = 0 with Q = 0). Predicted covariances are not exposed, so the backward pass replays predict's two in-place calls and documents that the replay is bit-identical.
Unsure: whether roundoff can violate the trace inequality on an ill-conditioned model; tests cover two benign models with a small numerical slack.
Verified: 1-D random walk matches a hand-written textbook recursion to 4.4e-16, 2-state model matches a try_inverse recursion, smoothed trace <= filtered at every tested step in f64 and f32; frozen 32, lib 105, new 16, doctests 13, build --all-targets green, clippy clean in new files.
